newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher after U.S. elections.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher after U.S. elections.

text.p: Tel Aviv stocks closed higher on Wednesday with rising turnover following the results of the U.S. elections, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.99 percent, or 1.85 points. to 189.37 on all share turnover of 61 million shekels against 46 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.15 percent to 199.33.
"The market rose today following the re-election of (U.S. President) Bill Clinton. Activity also rose but the market is still very weak," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
Bank Leumi rose 3.0 percent to 372. The bank said on Tuesday afternoon that it received three offers for the purchase of a controlling stake in its subsidiary Africa Israel Investments.

Tadiran fell 0.25 percent to 1,422 despite news that its subsidiary Tadiran Telecommunications posted third-quarter earnings per share of $0.36 against $0.21 a year earlier. Traders said the earnings, nevertheless, were somewhat disappointing and added that Tadiran was trading at a high price.
Maritime Bank surged the maximum 10 percent to 1,103 but traders said there was no evident reason for the rise.

"After two dull weeks activity has improved a little but the market is still far from a recovery. Nothing fundamental has changed in the economy. The interest rates are still high and the shekel is too strong," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
"The market was not surprised by the outcome of the U.S. elections but it has some impact on trading," Kolka said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 28,040 on volume of 6.8 million shekels; Clal Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 1,281 on volume of 4.0 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 1.5 percent to 826 on turnover of 3.9 million shekels.
